The Northern Gulf Coast bracing for the first hurricane of the Atlantic season.
The National Hurricane Center has posted a hurricane watch from the Louisiana-Mississippi
state line to Indian Pass and the Florida Panhandle, as NPR's Debbie Elliott reports.
National Hurricane Center Director Mike Brennan says ESA-ES is gaining steam as it moves over
the warm waters of the Gulf of Mexico.
ESA-ES is expected to be a strengthening, strong hurricane as it approaches the Northern
Gulf Coast on Friday into Friday night and Saturday.
You can see multiple life-threatening impacts from storm surge, heavy rainfall flooding,

Attorney Randy Spivey speaking to reporters Wednesday, saying Pyke has regained consciousness

46-year-old Jamal Howard was pronounced dead Wednesday evening after receiving the same

Howard's attorneys unsuccessfully sought to block the injection, arguing that he was intellectually

For the first time since 2002 an international democracy partnership will not send election
observers to monitor a US election.
The group says it has not been invited by the Trump administration.
Congressional Democrats say the move is another maneuver meant to undermine public trust in
the midterms, as NPR's Eric McDaniel reports.
The Trump administration's decision not to invite international observers to the United
States is, according to Jean Shaheen, top Democrat on the Senate Foreign Relations
Committee, "deeply antithetical to the spirit of freedom, democracy, and transparency that
defines our elections."
The news was first reported by Democracy Docket.
The Organization for Security and Cooperation in Europe regularly dispatches observers to
elections across the world.
Shaheen says she was an election monitor in the country of Georgia in 2012 and Bosnia and
Herzegovina in 2022.
White House spokeswoman Lauren Biss told NPR in a statement, "No other nation has done
more to advance the cause of human freedom and representative government.
Human elections will be administered, participated in, and observed by American citizens."
Eric McDaniel, NPR News, Washington.
This is NPR.
President Trump is due back at the White House after rallying voters in San Antonio with
Republican Senate candidate Ken Paxton.
Trump's trip to Texas was his third in less than a month as Republicans try to blunt Democratic
gains in key races.
Paxton is locked in a tight battle against Democrat James Tallarico.
His remarks, Trump's remarks, were interrupted by protesters multiple times.
A satirical statue of President Trump has been put up at the European Parliament in
Strasbourg, France.
The sculpture is meant to criticize the president's policies on climate change and what its Danish
creator calls a growing dominance of powerful nations.
Here's Terry Schultz reporting.
The eight-foot-high statue, titled The Orange Plague, depicts Trump completely naked holding
a golf club and a globe-shaped ball in one hand and scales in the other.
He's sitting on the shoulders of another man, who looks frail, and the whole thing
is covered in 23-karat gold leaf.
Danish artist Jens Galchiat says the work is inspired by the emperor's new clothes
and asks how long people will allow the powerful to be carried on their backs.
He says Trump was chosen as the subject because of his efforts to roll back climate initiatives
and to pressure other countries to do the same.
The statue was unveiled as part of a three-day exhibit hosted by Danish member of the European
Parliament, Per Klassen.
It's previously been displayed in Denmark, Germany and Brazil.
For NPR News, I'm Terry Schultz.
